questions.question: If the income of A is 10% more than that of B and the income of B is 20% less than that of C, then the respective incomes of A, B and C are in the ratio:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the income of C be 100 units.

Since B is 20% less than C, income of B = 100 − 20 = 80 units.

Since A is 10% more than B, income of A = 80 × 1.1 = 88 units.

Required ratio A : B : C = 88 : 80 : 100 = 22 : 20 : 25.

**∴ The correct answer is 22 : 20 : 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Income of A is 10% more than that of B.

Income of B is 20% less than that of C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/95e2260a6cb5b25947029870b1cf12cc17134b6d3e77026c56f2c8c1ee73471f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the income of C be 100x.

⇒ Income of B = 100x − (20% of 100x) = 80x

⇒ Income of A = 80x + (10% of 80x)

⇒ Income of A = 80x + 8x = 88x

⇒ The ratio of their incomes A : B : C = 88x : 80x : 100x

⇒ Dividing by the common factor 4x, we get:

⇒ A : B : C = 22 : 20 : 25

**∴ The correct answer is 22 : 20 : 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combining Ratios

If A : B = m : n and B : C = p : q, the combined ratio A : B : C can be found by making the common term B equal, resulting in (m × p) : (n × p) : (n × q).

Percentage to Ratio Conversion

Percentage changes can be written as fraction multipliers. For example, a 10% increase means multiplying by 11/10, and a 20% decrease means multiplying by 4/5. Using fractions makes ratio calculation much faster.

questions.question: Which among the following is the lowest computer storage size?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 Megabyte**__.

__
 
• **The megabyte is a multiple unit byte for digital content**__. Its recommended symbol for the unit is MB.

 __
 
• The unit prefix mega is a multiplier of** 1000000 (10⁶)** in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• One megabyte is then one million bytes of information. This description has been adopted in the International System of Quantities.
 
• The human genome consists of 800 MB DNA of details.
 
• The pieces that separate one human from another can be compressed to 4 MB.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The gigabyte **is a multiple unit byte for digital content. The Giga prefix is **10⁹** in the International System of Units (SI). As a consequence, one gigabyte is one billion bytes. The gigabyte unit symbol is GB.
 
• **The petabyte** is a **10¹⁵** byte digital content. The unit name of the petabyte is PB. The name is composed of the SI Peta prefix-composed by a non-SI byte unit.
 
• **A terabyte **is a multiple unit byte for digital content. The prefix tera reflects the fourth power of 1000, which is **10¹²** in the International System of Units (SI), and thus one terabyte is one trillion (short scale) bytes. The unit sign of the terabyte is TB.

questions.question: The sum of the ages of Sarala and Kishore is 26 years. If 3 years ago, Kishore was (3)/(2) times as old as Sarala, then the present age of Sarala is:

Sum of ages 3 years ago = 26 − (3 × 2) = 20 years.

Ratio of **Kishore** to **Sarala** (3 years ago) = 3 : 2.

Total units = 3 + 2 = 5 units → 20 years.

1 unit = 4 years ∴ **Sarala's** age (3 years ago) = 2 × 4 = 8 years.

Present age of **Sarala** = 8 + 3 = 11 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ (26 − S − 3) = 3/2 × (S − 3).

⇒ 2 × (23 − S) = 3 × (S − 3).

⇒ 46 − 2S = 3S − 9.

⇒ 5S = 55.

⇒ S = 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 years.**

Choose the most appropriate answer.

A jar contains a mixture of two liquids A and B in ratio 4:1. When 10 litre of the mixture is replaced with liquid B, the ratio becomes 2:3. How many litres of liquid A was present in the jar initially?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Ratio **A : B** = 4 : 1

After replacing 10L mixture with **B**, New Ratio = 2 : 3

Since only **B** is added, **A** must remain constant: (2 : 3) × 2 = 4 : 6

Change in **B** units = 6 − 1 = 5 units → 10 L | 1 unit = 2 L

Total mixture (Final) = (4 + 6) × 2 = 20 L | Initial **A** = 20 × (4/5) = 16 L

**∴ The correct answer is 16 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/654d940af882d32c223fc24564d9078c05f9cc3e116c997c813f0272c0e0dd8a.png] 

Let the initial quantity of **Liquid A** and **Liquid B** be 4x and 1x respectively.

Total initial mixture = 5x

When 10 L of mixture is removed:

⇒ Quantity of **A** removed = 10 × (4/5) = 8 L

⇒ Quantity of **B** removed = 10 × (1/5) = 2 L

New quantities after adding 10 L of **Liquid B**:

⇒ **A** = 4x − 8

⇒ **B** = x − 2 + 10 = x + 8

According to the question, New Ratio = 2 : 3

⇒ (4x − 8) / (x + 8) = 2 / 3

⇒ 3(4x − 8) = 2(x + 8)

⇒ 12x − 24 = 2x + 16

⇒ 10x = 40

⇒ x = 4

⇒ Initial quantity of **Liquid A** = 4x = 4 × 4 = 16 L

**∴ The correct answer is 16 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mixture Replacement Rule

When a part of mixture is replaced by one of the liquids, the quantity of the liquid not added remains constant in ratio terms if adjusted properly.

Removal of Mixture

When mixture is removed, the components are removed in the same ratio as their concentration: Removed Amount of A = Total Removed × (A / Total Ratio).

Final Quantity Formula

Final Quantity = Initial Quantity × (1 − Replacement Volume / Total Volume)ⁿ, used specifically for repeated identical replacements.</p

questions.question: The speed of a train is 42 km/h. It crosses an electric pole in 27 seconds and a platform in 51 seconds. What is the length (in m) of the platform?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **extra time** taken to cross the platform instead of the pole is directly due to the **length of the platform**.

Extra time = 51 sec − 27 sec = 24 sec.

Speed in m/s = 42 × (5/18) = 35/3 m/s.

Length of platform = Speed × Extra time = (35/3) × 24 = 35 × 8 = 280 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 280 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Speed** of the train = 42 km/h

Time to cross **electric pole** (T₁) = 27 sec

Time to cross **platform** (T₂) = 51 sec

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Speed (m/s) = Speed (km/h) × (5/18)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d36b1682eec8a478d6f5f3bab413ba59c3da43ecb2bcdaca80833de109fc1fa2.png] 

⇒ Speed in m/s = 42 × (5/18) = 35/3 m/s

⇒ Length of train (L) = Speed × Time to cross pole

⇒ L = (35/3) × 27 = 35 × 9 = 315 m

⇒ Total distance to cross platform = Length of train + Length of platform (P)

⇒ L + P = Speed × Time to cross platform

⇒ 315 + P = (35/3) × 51

⇒ 315 + P = 35 × 17

⇒ 315 + P = 595

⇒ P = 595 − 315 = 280 m

**∴ The correct answer is 280 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing a Point Object

When a train crosses an electric pole, a tree, or a stationary person, the distance covered is equal to the **length of the train**.

Train Crossing a Large Object

When a train crosses a platform, a bridge, or another stationary train, the distance covered is equal to the **Sum of the lengths** of the train and the object.</p

questions.question: By selling 24 pens, a vendor lost the selling price of 6 pens. Find the loss percent

Let the **Selling Price (SP)** of 1 pen be 1 unit.

Total **SP** of 24 pens = 24 units.

**Loss** = SP of 6 pens = 6 units.

**Cost Price (CP)** = SP + Loss = 24 + 6 = 30 units.

**Loss %** = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100 = (6 ÷ 30) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Let SP of 1 pen = x.

⇒ Loss = 6x.

⇒ CP of 24 pens = SP + Loss = 24x + 6x = 30x.

⇒ Loss% = (6x ÷ 30x) × 100.

⇒ Loss% = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

Concept of Profit in terms of SP

questions.question: Anil sells a table to Kamal at a profit of 10% and Kamal sells it to Rajat at a profit of 12%. If Rajat pays ₹ 246.40 for it, then how much had Anil paid for it?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Ratio Method**: Profit 10% = 10 → 11 and Profit 12% = 25 → 28 (since 12/100 = 3/25).

Combined Ratio of **Initial CP** to **Final SP** = (10 × 25) : (11 × 28) = 250 : 308.

Given 308 units = ₹ 246.40 ⇒ 1 unit = 246.40 ÷ 308 = 0.8.

**Anil's CP** = 250 units × 0.8 = ₹ 200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit of **Anil** = 10%

Profit of **Kamal** = 12%

Price paid by **Rajat** = ₹ 246.40

**Formula Used:**

Final Price = Initial Price × (1 + P₁/100) × (1 + P₂/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3ac8d7f4a7063c0dfb1ebaed89f6fe9c9dced9ae2d9b4e4cf86811a275c113e9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the cost price for **Anil** be **x**.

⇒ Selling price for **Anil** (Cost for **Kamal**) = x × (110/100) = 1.1x

⇒ Selling price for **Kamal** (Cost for **Rajat**) = 1.1x × (112/100)

⇒ 246.40 = 1.1x × 1.12

⇒ 246.40 = 1.232x

⇒ x = 246.40 ÷ 1.232

⇒ x = 200

∴ **Anil** had paid ₹ 200 for the table. This corresponds to **Option 3**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Profit/Loss Formula

The overall percentage change for two successive changes of a% and b% is given by [a + b + (ab/100)]%.

Cost Price from Selling Price

If an item is sold at a profit of P%, then Cost Price (CP) = [100 ÷ (100 + P)] × Selling Price (SP).

Chain Rule in Profit and Loss

When an item passes through multiple hands, the final price = Initial CP × (100 + g₁)/100 × (100 + g₂)/100 ... where g is the gain/loss percentage at each step.

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 8,500 amounts to Rs. 11,900 in 5 years at simple interest per annum. If the rate of interest is increased by 3%, then the increased amount for the same period is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Extra interest earned due to 3% rate hike = **Principal** × **Rate Increase** × **Time** / 100.

Extra Interest = 8,500 × 3 × 5 / 100 = ₹1,275.

New Amount = **Original Amount** + **Extra Interest** = 11,900 + 1,275 = ₹13,175.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13,175.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹8,500

**Amount (A)** = ₹11,900

**Time (T)** = 5 years

**Rate Increase** = 3%

**Formula Used:**

**Simple Interest (SI)** = (P × R × T) / 100

**Amount (A)** = Principal + Simple Interest

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f1efc6f00780ebbe07abd680c50598b6cdca7bdc1e0ecaea70c7a0cfec1331b4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Simple Interest (SI)** = 11,900 − 8,500 = ₹3,400

⇒ **Rate (R)** = (3,400 × 100) / (8,500 × 5) = 8%

⇒ **New Rate** = 8% + 3% = 11%

⇒ **New SI** = (8,500 × 11 × 5) / 100 = ₹4,675

⇒ **New Amount** = 8,500 + 4,675 = ₹13,175

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13,175.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Properties

**Simple Interest** is calculated only on the initial **Principal** amount for every period. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) / 100.

Effect of Rate Change

If the **Rate** increases by x%, the **Interest** increases by (P × x × T) / 100. This can be directly added to the old **Amount**.

Amount Formula

The **Amount** is the sum of the **Principal** and the **Interest** earned over the **Time Period**. A = P × (1 + RT/100).

Ratio of **Length : Breadth** = 3 : 1. Diagonal ratio = √(3² + 1²) = √10.

√10 units = 20 m ⇒ 1 unit = 20/√10 = 2√10 m.

**Perimeter** = 2 × (3 + 1) units = 8 units = 8 × 2√10 = 16√10 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 16√10 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Speed = 0.5 kmph, Time = 144 sec, Length (L) = 3 × Breadth (B).

**Formula Used:** Distance = Speed × Time; Diagonal (D) = √(L² + B²); Perimeter (P) = 2(L + B).

⇒ 400 = 9x² + x² = 10x²

⇒ x² = 40 ⇒ x = √40 = 2√10 m.

⇒ **Perimeter** = 2(3x + x) = 8x

⇒ **Perimeter** = 8 × 2√10 = 16√10 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 16√10 m.**

Rectangle Properties

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Substitution Method:** Assume a specific value for **θ** to simplify the expression quickly.

Let **θ = 45°**. We know that **tan 45° = 1**, **sec 45° = √2**, **cot 45° = 1**, and **cosec 45° = √2**.

Substitute these values into the expression: (1 + 1 − √2)(1 + 1 + √2)

⇒ (2 − √2)(2 + √2) = 2² − (√2)²

⇒ 4 − 2 = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The expression (1 + tan θ − sec θ)(1 + cot θ + cosec θ)

**Formula Used:** tan θ = sin θ/cos θ | cot θ = cos θ/sin θ | sec θ = 1/cos θ | cosec θ = 1/sin θ

⇒ (1 + sin θ/cos θ − 1/cos θ) × (1 + cos θ/sin θ + 1/sin θ)

⇒ [(cos θ + sin θ − 1) / cos θ] × [(sin θ + cos θ + 1) / sin θ]

⇒ [(sin θ + cos θ) − 1] [(sin θ + cos θ) + 1] / (sin θ cos θ)

Using the algebraic identity **(a − b)(a + b) = a² − b²**:

⇒ [(sin θ + cos θ)² − 1²] / (sin θ cos θ)

⇒ (sin² θ + cos² θ + 2 sin θ cos θ − 1) / (sin θ cos θ)

Since **sin² θ + cos² θ = 1**:

⇒ (1 + 2 sin θ cos θ − 1) / (sin θ cos θ)

⇒ (2 sin θ cos θ) / (sin θ cos θ)

⇒ 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include **sin² θ + cos² θ = 1**, **1 + tan² θ = sec² θ**, and **1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ**.

Reciprocal Relations

Recall that **cosec θ = 1/sin θ**, **sec θ = 1/cos θ**, and **cot θ = 1/tan θ** are essential for simplification.

questions.question: If (5)/(2) is a root of the equation 4x² - mx + 25 = 0, then the value of m is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since **x = 5/2** (or 2.5) is a **root** of the equation, it must satisfy the **quadratic equation**.

Substitute **x = 2.5** directly into 4x² − mx + 25 = 0.

4(2.5)² − 2.5m + 25 = 0

25 − 2.5m + 25 = 0 ⇒ 50 = 2.5m

m = 50 ÷ 2.5 = 20.

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Quadratic equation 4x² − mx + 25 = 0 and one root **x = 5/2**.

To find the **value of m**, substitute the value of the root in the given equation:

⇒ 4(5/2)² − m(5/2) + 25 = 0

⇒ 4 × (25 / 4) − 5m / 2 + 25 = 0

⇒ 25 − 5m / 2 + 25 = 0

⇒ 50 − 5m / 2 = 0

⇒ 5m / 2 = 50

⇒ 5m = 50 × 2

⇒ 5m = 100

⇒ m = 100 ÷ 5

⇒ m = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Roots of an Equation

A value **k** is called a **root** of the equation f(x) = 0 if and only if f(k) = 0. Substituting the root satisfies the equation.

Sum and Product of Roots

For a **quadratic equation** ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is **−b/a** and the product of roots is **c/a**.

Discriminant and Nature of Roots

The term **D = b² − 4ac** is the **discriminant**. If D > 0, roots are real and distinct; if D = 0, roots are real and equal; if D < 0, roots are imaginary.

Standard Form

A **quadratic equation** is typically expressed in the form **ax² + bx + c = 0**, where a, b, and c are constants and a ≠ 0.</p

questions.question: A man earns a profit of 45 percent by selling a bike for a certain price. If he sells that bike at double the price, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the bike be 100 units.

Selling Price (SP) at 45% profit = 100 + 45 = 145 units.

New SP when sold at double the price = 2 × 145 = 290 units.

New Profit = New SP − CP = 290 − 100 = 190 units.

Since the base CP is 100 units, the profit percentage is directly the profit amount.

**∴ The correct answer is 190%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial profit percentage = 45%

New Selling Price = 2 × Initial Selling Price

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/90b9a6846371864149e30d5fa1d627c2df919edb190e25b3ee31a3d6ae01c63a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the bike be x.

⇒ Initial Selling Price (SP) = x × (100 + 45) ÷ 100 = 1.45x

⇒ New Selling Price = 2 × Initial SP = 2 × 1.45x = 2.90x

⇒ New Profit = New Selling Price − CP

⇒ New Profit = 2.90x − x = 1.90x

⇒ New Profit % = (New Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ New Profit % = (1.90x ÷ x) × 100 = 190%

**∴ The correct answer is 190%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

MP is the price printed on the article. Discount is always calculated on the MP. Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Profit

When an article is sold sequentially by multiple sellers, the effective SP is calculated cumulatively: Final SP = CP × (100 + P₁%) ÷ 100 × (100 + P₂%) ÷ 100.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer professes to sell goods at CP but uses a false weight, the profit percentage is calculated as: Profit % = (Error ÷ (True Value − Error)) × 100.

questions.question: Pipe A and pipe B can fill a tank alone in 6 and 8 hours respectively and pipe C can empty the same tank in 12 hours. If all three pipes are opened at the same time then in how many time the tank will be filled?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total tank capacity = LCM(6, 8, 12) = 24 units.

Combined efficiency = (24 ÷ 6) + (24 ÷ 8) − (24 ÷ 12) = 4 + 3 − 2 = 5 units/hr.

Time taken to fill = Total capacity ÷ Combined efficiency = 24 ÷ 5 = 4.8 hours.

0.8 hours in minutes = 0.8 × 60 = 48 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hours 48 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by pipe A to fill the tank = 6 hours

Time taken by pipe B to fill the tank = 8 hours

Time taken by pipe C to empty the tank = 12 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Capacity = LCM of individual times

Efficiency = Total Capacity ÷ Time

Total Time = Total Capacity ÷ Total Efficiency

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (hrs)**
 **Total Capacity**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A (Inlet)
 6
 24
 24 ÷ 6 = +4
 
 

 B (Inlet)
 8
 24 ÷ 8 = +3
 
 

 C (Outlet)
 12
 24 ÷ 12 = −2
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency when all pipes are open = +4 + 3 − 2 = 5 units/hr

⇒ Time required to fill the tank = 24 ÷ 5 = 4.8 hours

⇒ Converting the decimal part into minutes = 0.8 × 60 = 48 minutes

⇒ Total time required = 4 hours 48 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hours 48 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Base Concept

If a pipe fills a tank in x hours, its work done per hour is +1/x. If an outlet pipe empties it in y hours, its work done per hour is −1/y.

Combined Work Rule

The net efficiency of multiple pipes operating simultaneously is the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies. Inlet pipes contribute positive work, while outlet pipes represent negative work.

Time Conversion

To convert fractional or decimal hours into minutes, simply multiply the decimal fraction by 60. Example: 0.25 hours = 0.25 × 60 = 15 minutes.

questions.question: In a row of 51 students, facing north, Tinu is 24th from the left end. If Shivangi is 11th to the right of Tinu, what is Shivangi's position from the right end of the row?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total students = 51

Tinu's position from left = 24th

Shivangi's position to the right of Tinu = 11th

**Calculations:**

Shivangi's position from left = Tinu's position from left + Shivangi's position to the right of Tinu

⇒ Shivangi's position from left = 24 + 11 = 35th

Shivangi's position from right = Total students - Shivangi's position from left + 1

⇒ Shivangi's position from right = 51 - 35 + 1 = 17th

**∴ Shivangi's position from the right end of the row is 17th.**

questions.question: Two poles are standing on the ground. The distances between their feet and their tops are 48 m and 50 m respectively. If the height of the small pole is 10 m, find the height of the big pole.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Pythagorean triplet** (7, 24, 25) scaled by a factor of 2: (14, 48, 50).

The distance between feet (Base) is 48 m and the distance between tops (Hypotenuse) is 50 m.

Thus, the **difference in height** (Perpendicular) must be 14 m.

Height of the **big pole** = Height of **small pole** + **Difference** = 10 + 14 = 24 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of small pole (h₁) = 10 m

Distance between feet (d) = 48 m

Distance between tops (s) = 50 m

**Formula Used:**

According to **Pythagorean Theorem**: s² = d² + (h₂ − h₁)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b35b6b7419d52bb7e23648829911f11b8218c3152aed38c463e1ad08a38ead13.png] 

Let the height of the **big pole** be h₂.

⇒ (h₂ − 10)² + 48² = 50²

⇒ (h₂ − 10)² = 50² − 48²

⇒ (h₂ − 10)² = (50 − 48)(50 + 48)

⇒ (h₂ − 10)² = 2 × 98 = 196

⇒ h₂ − 10 = √196

⇒ h₂ − 10 = 14

⇒ h₂ = 14 + 10 = 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Triplets

These are sets of three positive integers a, b, and c such that a² + b² = c². Common triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25). Any multiple of a triplet is also a triplet.

Application in Heights

When two parallel vertical objects stand on horizontal ground, the **slant distance** between their tops, the **horizontal distance** between their bases, and the **difference in their heights** always form a **right-angled triangle**.

Algebraic Identity

Using the identity a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) simplifies calculations involving squares of large numbers, especially in geometry problems.</p

questions.question: The sum of the three sides of a cuboid is 20 cm and the sum of the squares of the three sides is 150 cm. Find the total surface area of the cuboid?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Surface Area (TSA) = (Sum of three sides)² − (Sum of squares of three sides)

Sum of sides = 20 cm

Sum of squares = 150 cm²

TSA = 20² − 150 = 400 − 150 = 250 cm²

**∴ The correct option is D.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Sum of sides (l + b + h) = 20 cm

Sum of squares (l² + b² + h²) = 150 cm²

Formula Used: (l + b + h)² = l² + b² + h² + 2(lb + bh + hl)

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2(lb + bh + hl)

 
 

 

 Length (l)
 Breadth (b)
 Height (h)
 TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl)

⇒ (l + b + h)² = (l² + b² + h²) + TSA
⇒ (20)² = 150 + TSA
⇒ 400 = 150 + TSA
⇒ TSA = 400 − 150
⇒ TSA = 250 cm²

**∴ The correct option is D.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cuboid

The total space occupied by the cuboid is given by the product of its three dimensions: Volume = l × b × h.

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The length of the longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid is its diagonal: Diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²).

Lateral Surface Area (LSA)

The surface area of the four vertical faces (excluding top and bottom) is: LSA = 2 × h × (l + b).

Relation between TSA and Diagonal

Total Surface Area = (Sum of Dimensions)² − (Diagonal)².</p
